summary: Regression-tested the additive 7-index change (teams.org_id/setting_id, org_settings.org_id, focus_topics.org_id, standards_documents.org_id, users.team_id/setting_id). Verified index existence + validity + planner usage via pg_indexes/EXPLAIN, then ran 32 API tests (2 new pytest suites) across admin.list_users, org_settings/teams CRUD, assign-team, /org/structure, team-insights, registers, people-stats, dashboard, focus-topics CRUD, standards documents, plus a purpose-built team-scoped-manager isolation suite. Also drove the UI (PeopleHub People/Structure tabs, Team Insights team+setting filters, Settings > Focus Topics, Standards Library) as admin via injected cookies. Result: ZERO regressions attributable to the index change (31/32 API tests pass, all reads return correct scoped data). Two PRE-EXISTING defects surfaced during the regression sweep (one backend 500 on branch rename, one stale-list-after-mutation UI bug) — neither is caused by the indexes but both are user-facing.

critical.issue: Always 500. org.py:213 does existing['manager_user_id'] but the org_settings table has NO manager_user_id column (actual columns: id, org_id, name, settings, created_at, updated_at) -> KeyError: 'manager_user_id'. Every branch/setting rename from Organisation > Structure fails. PRE-EXISTING (not caused by the index change). Fix: add the column via init_db.py idempotent ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS manager_user_id TEXT (create_setting/update_setting already assume it) or remove the manager_user_id logic. Note get_structure() only survives because it uses dict.get().

minor.issue: 2.8s p50 (other endpoints ~1.55s incl. auth+network RTT). Classic N+1: one query per setting for teams, then per team for supervisor name + members. Consider 3 batched queries (settings, teams WHERE setting_id = ANY, users WHERE team_id = ANY).
3.5s p50 for an org with 15 users / few meetings — worth profiling before data grows.
Orphan row teams.name='Team Alpha' with setting_id=NULL is unreachable from the UI (/org/structure only lists teams by setting_id) and from team filters. Pre-existing seed residue.

ui_bugs.issue: Add / Set-current a focus topic shows the success toast but the list is NOT updated: load() uses cachedGet('/prep/focus-topics') with a 5-min TTL and invalidateCache() is never called after POST/PUT. Reproduced: DB row TEST_UI_Focus_iter97 created, UI kept showing 'No focus topics yet' until reload. PRE-EXISTING.

Creating a branch (Add Setting) or team shows 'Setting created'/'Team created' and the row IS persisted server-side, but the tree frequently does not show it — 3 of 5 attempts never refreshed even after 15s; only a full page reload showed it. Additionally the page-header 'Refresh' button fires NO network request (served from the 60s apiCache entry), so the user cannot recover in-app. refreshData() invalidates then calls fetchData() without awaiting/serialising, and the slow (2.8s) /org/structure refetch appears to race with a re-populated cache entry. PRE-EXISTING.

No data-testid on the per-branch/per-team edit / delete / Add Team action buttons, so the rename path (the endpoint that 500s) is not reachable by automated tests without brittle hover+nth-button probing. Please add data-testid="edit-setting-btn-{id}", "delete-setting-btn-{id}", "add-team-btn-{id}".

integration_issues.issue: POST succeeds (200) and a GET /org/structure follows, but the rendered tree keeps the pre-create list; in-page fetch('/api/org/structure') confirmed the server was already correct, so the staleness is purely client-side.
Stale cachedGet response served after mutation (no invalidateCache in FocusTopicsTab).

issues: Header says '7 staff members' while the People & Usage stat card says '10 Total staff' (header appears to exclude the 3 invite-pending users) — inconsistent counts on the same screen.

action_items: CRITICAL: fix PUT /api/org/settings/{id} 500 — add org_settings.manager_user_id column (idempotent ALTER in init_db.py) or drop the manager_user_id references in org.py create_setting/update_setting/get_structure.
HIGH: add invalidateCache('/prep/focus-topics') (or a live refetch) after focus-topic POST/PUT/DELETE in OrgSettings.js FocusTopicsTab.
HIGH: make OrgStructure.js post-mutation refresh deterministic (await invalidate+fetch, or force a cache-bypassing GET) and make the header Refresh button bypass apiCache.
LOW: add data-testid to branch/team edit/delete/Add-Team buttons in OrgStructure.js; clean up orphan teams row with setting_id NULL.
critical_code_review_comments: org.py:213 indexes an asyncpg Record by a column that does not exist in the schema — such column access should be schema-verified; init_db.py adds indexes for org_settings but never the manager_user_id column the code assumes.

utils/apiCache.js gives every cacheable GET a module-level TTL, but several mutation handlers (FocusTopicsTab, and the Refresh button paths) never invalidate, so the UI can display stale data for up to 5 minutes with no user-visible recovery other than a reload. Consider a helper that wraps mutate+invalidate+refetch.

The index change itself is clean: purely CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS inside init_db.py's idempotent block; verified all 7 indexes exist, are indisvalid, and are chosen by the planner (EXPLAIN with enable_seqscan=off shows Index/Bitmap Index Scan on each of the 7 columns).

success_rate.backend: 97% (31/32 API assertions passed; the single failure is the pre-existing PUT /org/settings 500)
success_rate.frontend: 70% (staff list, team/setting insight filters, structure tree read, standards library all OK; branch/team create refresh + focus-topic list refresh stale)

Verified post-run DB state restored to pre-test baseline (org_settings = ['Team one','Team Two'], teams = [('Team Alpha', NULL)], focus_topics = empty, manager@ and jane@ team_id/setting_id back to NULL). manager@supervision.com password hash was stale (401) and was re-hashed to Manager123! via tests/reset_test_pw.py.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Index change itself is fully verified — no need to re-test it. Re-run `python3 -m pytest tests/test_iter97_index_regression.py tests/test_iter97_scoped_manager.py -p no:randomly -o addopts=''` after the org_settings.manager_user_id fix; test_03_update_setting is the only expected failure today. Suites take ~3 min because every login costs ~1.5s and MFA is DB-overridden. If logins start returning 401 'Invalid credentials' run tests/reset_test_pw.py, and if they return 429 run tests/clear_rate_limit.py. For UI testing, inject cookies from tests/get_tokens.py (tokens live 30 min). Note the org has ZERO standards_documents rows, so 'existing parsed custom standards doc still usable in prep/rescan' could only be verified at endpoint level (GET /admin/standards/documents = 200 empty list, GET /prep/{id}/context = 200); upload a doc first if you need end-to-end coverage there.
rca_of_the_issue: Index change: safe — 7 indexes created idempotently by init_db.py on backend startup, all present, indisvalid, and used by the planner; no query logic/RLS/columns touched and every scoped read (org / team / setting) returned identical, correctly-filtered data, including the security-sensitive team-scoped manager isolation (manager saw exactly its 2 in-scope users, ?ignore_scope=true correctly ignored, and 403 on out-of-scope branch/team creation). Unrelated defects found: (1) PUT /api/org/settings/{id} raises KeyError 'manager_user_id' because org.py assumes a column absent from org_settings, so branch rename always 500s; (2) the React apiCache module serves stale cached GETs after mutations in FocusTopicsTab (no invalidation at all) and, intermittently, in OrgStructure (invalidate+refetch races with the 2.8s /org/structure request and the Refresh button never hits the network), so newly created branches/teams/topics appear only after a page reload even though they are persisted.
